narrative.overview:
Kivox's visual language is built around a single conviction: the site itself is the portfolio. Every pixel demonstrates the craft, clarity, and warmth the studio promises to deliver. The aesthetic draws from the intimacy of a well-lit workshop at dusk; warm amber light pooling across dark surfaces, the confidence of tools laid out with intention, materials that feel honest rather than polished to anonymity.

The system is Committed: warm amber carries 30–60% of visual weight at hero moments, CTAs, and section transitions, while warm-tinted neutrals ground everything else. There is no pure black, no pure white, no cold gray anywhere in the palette. Every neutral is shifted toward the amber hue family at chroma 0.005–0.02, creating a cohesion that feels inevitable rather than decorated.

This system explicitly rejects generic SaaS template sites, loud startup pages, dark tech aesthetics with neon accents, enterprise posturing, and luxury hotel minimalism. If a visitor could mistake this for a template, the design has failed.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-tinted neutrals in every surface (hue 55–85, chroma 0.005–0.02)
Committed amber accent at key moments, restrained everywhere else
Editorial serif/sans pairing (Spectral + Bricolage Grotesque) for headline variety
Structural shadows with amber-tinted hover states
Scroll-driven section crossfades (overdrive system) for cinematic pacing
Dual-theme: warm parchment (light) and firelit dark, both fully warm-tinted

rules.name: The Warm Tint Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in both themes carries chroma 0.005–0.02 toward the amber hue family (H 55–85). Pure #000, #fff, and #808080 are forbidden. The warmth is the identity.

rules.name: The Committed Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only chromatic color in site chrome. It carries 30–60% of visual weight at hero moments, CTAs, and section transitions, then retreats to ≤10% in content-heavy sections.

rules.name: The POV Wash Rule
rules.body: The philosophical section and services use a committed amber-tinted environmental wash that shifts between oklch(0.90 0.06 62) in light and oklch(0.09 0.025 60) in dark.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Headlines use Bricolage Grotesque (confident craft), subheads use Spectral (editorial warmth), body uses Figtree (clear readability). Never substitute one for another.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: All numeric data uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums via the studio-tabular utility. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: All headings use text-wrap: balance. All prose uses text-wrap: pretty. Non-negotiable.

rules.name: The Warm Response Rule
rules.body: Shadows are neutral at rest and warm on interaction. The transition from colorless depth to amber-tinted glow is the fundamental feedback pattern.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: The carousel frame uses 5 shadow layers including inset shadows. No other component may approach this shadow complexity.

dos: Do tint every neutral toward hue 55–85 at chroma 0.005–0.02.
Do use OKLCH as the canonical color format. Reduce chroma as lightness approaches 0 or 100.
Do apply text-wrap: balance on all headings and text-wrap: pretty on all prose.
Do increase body line-height from 1.6 to 1.65 in dark mode.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for all numeric data.
Do use the studio-eyebrow class for all section labels. Bracket format: [ Label ].
Do ease out with exponential curves (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion with instant fallbacks.
Do use the studio-surface utility for card containers.
Do pair Bricolage Grotesque headlines with Spectral italic for the key emotional word.
donts: Don't use pure black (#000), pure white (#fff), or any un-tinted gray.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default surface treatment.
Don't use side-stripe borders (colored border-left/right > 1px as accents).
Don't create hero-metric templates (big number, small label, supporting stats).
Don't build identical card grids (same-sized cards with icon + heading + text repeated).
Don't use neon colors, aggressive animations, or hype language.
Don't use awards/metrics claims, corporate jargon, or defensive disclaimers.
Don't use em dashes in copy.
Don't restate headings or write intros that repeat the title.
Don't use modals as a first thought.
Don't animate CSS layout properties. Use transform and opacity only.
Don't use Inter, Space Grotesk, or any geometric grotesque as a substitute for Bricolage Grotesque.
